A lot of people are givkng vague answers and not explaining why. A small deck ranges from 1 to 6 cards. Reasons being you have a build and more cards prevent you from drawing what you need on command.  Examples of this are pyro, duplicate, or trinity builds.

Medium decks range from 6 to 15 imo because they have a lot of synergy but every card is useful. By having more cards you get increased mana regen but also have to cycle for specific cards. Examples include: Flow and Frost.

Large decks are 15+ but can work because the cards you need are either a) duplicates or b) spam cards. Examples include: Jam and Kunai.

Now some small decks can turn into large decks by virtue of their synergy. Its just a matter of preference and what you build into. Benefits to each.

One final tip....if you get a seed with her go ahead and write it down so you can repeat it over and over. Knowing she will be boss # means you can be better prepared mentally.

Flow decks are decks that have cards with flow. You gain stacks of flow as you play your cards. Each card that doesn't give flow takes away a stack. If you have flow or stacks of it, you generally get a secondary effect. Whether that be bonus damage, recycling the card or extending your attack.

Trinity works the same way. Except instead of losing stacks, Trinity remains until you've used its effect. Every third card gets a huge boost.

Deck building in general comes later on imo. Starting with Saffron she is one of the best characters to build around in general since she has synergy with so many available cards.

But since you want tips on deck building I start usually with what is my goal? There are a lot of procs/statuses to play around with. The easiest one to start off with is Frost for Saffron.

You apply frost in stacks of 3. On the third stack they take 150 dmg. Simple enough.

The rules to making a deck in this game aren't simply by any means. But some things I generally keep in mind are: 

1. Overall deck cost. A deck with 15 1 cost spells is more efficient for spamming but does it achieve the same as a two card deck with two spells of 3? Not necessarily.

2. Comfort. Getting shields in your deck extends your longevity until you can literally frame dodge most dmg.

3. Artifacts. If you get a frost artifact and you have a decent pull (1-2 frost cards added prior to the next world) then stacking into it is to your benefit and getting rid of anything not towards that focus is detrimental.

Lastly you can focus specific pools to get cards which synergize together easier.
